abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of ovarian tumors during pregnancy can be challenging because of the risk of fetal wastage and the possibility of surgery-related complications, or a delayed diagnosis of a possibly lethal disease or malignancy. The aim of this study was to study the characteristics and outcomes of pregnant women undergoing surgical intervention for ovarian tumors during pregnancy. METHODS: We reviewed the data of 102 pregnant women who underwent ovarian surgery between 2000 and 2010 at Taipei Veterans General Hospital, Taiwan. Data subject to analysis included gestational age at the time of surgery, complications, surgical and pathological findings, and the outcome of pregnancy. RESULTS: Fifty-two women who underwent surgery were excluded, whether by cesarean section, during the postpartum period or during simultaneous abortion surgery. Ultimately, the data of 50 patients were analyzed. Almost all patients (n = 46, 92%) were asymptomatic and underwent elective surgery. Frequently, this surgery was done in the second trimester (n = 35, 70%). We determined that teratoma (26%), mucinous cystadenomas (20%), and endometriomas (16%) were the three most common pathological findings. Nonspecific ovarian tumors were common (28%), including seven corpus luteum cysts, six simple cysts, and one paratubal cyst. Two women were diagnosed with malignant ovarian tumors, but both were metastatic and the primary site was the colon. Ten women underwent laparoscopic surgery. General anesthesia was used in four patients, and all underwent emergency exploratory laparotomy. There was no surgery-related complication or instance of preterm labor. CONCLUSION: In our study cohort, surgical intervention during pregnancy was safe, since neither surgical approach, such as exploratory laparotomy or laparoscopic surgery, nor anesthesia methods, for example general anesthesia or spinal anesthesia showed negative impact on the pregnancy outcomes. Reported cases of malignant ovarian tumor are still rare, thus, the possibility of metastatic tumor should be considered first.
abstract_ja: 背景：妊娠中の卵巣腫瘍の治療は、流産のリスク、手術関連合併症、または致死的疾患や悪性腫瘍の診断遅延の可能性があるため困難を伴う。本研究の目的は、妊娠中に卵巣腫瘍に対する外科的治療を受けた妊婦の特徴と転帰を検討することである。方法：2000年から2010年の間に台湾の台北榮民總醫院で妊娠中に卵巣手術を受けた102例の妊婦のデータを後ろ向きに調べた。解析対象は、手術時の妊娠週数、合併症、手術および病理所見、妊娠転帰とした。結果：帝王切開、産褥期、または同時の人工妊娠中絶手術に伴い手術を受けた52例は除外した。最終的に50例のデータを解析した。ほぼ全例（46例、92%）が無症状で、選択的手術を受けた。手術は妊娠中期（35例、70%）に行われることが多かった。最も多い病理所見は奇形腫（26%）、粘液性嚢胞腺腫（20%）、子宮内膜症（16%）の3つであった。非特異的な卵巣腫瘍も多く（28%）、黄体嚢胞7例、単純嚢胞6例、傍卵管嚢胞1例を含んだ。悪性卵巣腫瘍と診断された2例は、いずれも転移性で原発巣は大腸であった。10例が腹腔鏡手術を受けた。全身麻酔は4例に用いられ、全例が緊急開腹探索術を受けた。手術関連合併症や早産は認められなかった。結論：本コホートでは、妊娠中の手術介入は安全であった。開腹探索術や腹腔鏡手術といった手術手技、また全身麻酔や脊髄麻酔といった麻酔法のいずれも、妊娠転帰に悪影響を示さなかった。悪性卵巣腫瘍の報告は依然として稀であるため、転移性腫瘍の可能性を第一に考慮すべきである。
